purpose: SpaceFace animation reference pack — lead-reviewed Grok reference_to_video clips as Blender rigid-part motion targets. Design references only; not runtime animations.
sourceVersionNotes: During collection, commit a66c602b4 republished the same Forge bodies with v2 shared hull plating and look tuning. Captured source GLB hashes identify the original render inputs; the frozen PNG and movie hashes remain authoritative reference provenance. Use the current Forge source geometry/materials for animation builds and re-review identity if a structural model change occurs. Do not replace the captured hashes with newer asset bytes.

notes.sourceParts: sourceParts locators are prefix families, not new rig guarantees
notes.scopeSource: Mechanism close-ups are scoped animation references with actual whole-model image context. They do not certify a whole-asset animation or replace current Forge geometry and materials.
notes.review: accepted/scopes/notes/phaseLandmarks copied verbatim from lead-authored ANIMATION_REFERENCE_REVIEW.json (preserved at .devshots/animation-references/lead-review.json); timestamps = (frame-1)/24 at native CFR 24fps.
notes.recovery: The input/video receipts survived a local cleanup. Media was recovered byte-for-byte. The source-locator catalog and complete build/review program were restored and re-authored by the lead before publication.

entries.prompt: Use the exact spacecraft from the pinned frame and keep its entire teal pressure hull, long flat cyan-and-charcoal roof rail, both broad shoulder sponsons, green repair box and rear drum motionless. entries.title: Wasp seam rupture and rigid debris handoff
entries.proposedGeometry: Wasp-specific substantial rupture fragments derived from its actual source; simulation owns actor trajectories and mass conservation.
entries.prompt: Use the exact Wasp spacecraft from the opening model render in a locked overhead three-quarter shot. A compact bright internal rupture splits its centre into a few substantial rigid pieces: the recognizable bow/canopy portion, rear drive portion and original side or tail plates separate along believable structural seams, retaining their original surfaces, proportions and livery as they drift apart slowly in zero gravity. Keep the breakup legible and weighted, with a short internal flash and sparse small chips rather than a smoke cloud or a replacement spaceship; the camera and background remain fixed and the original hull is clearly identifiable in the pieces. End with the separated pieces still in frame, showing the torn seams and attachments; this is an art reference for an immediate game-physics handoff, not permission to delay a kill or bake gameplay trajectories.
